documents.title: Q4 Product Strategy & Collaborative Workspace RFC
documents.content:
Q4 Product Strategy: Next-Generation Collaborative Docs

Welcome to the Ajaia Collaborative Editor specification document. This document outlines our product vision, core customer pain points, and engineering execution roadmap for Q4.

1. Executive Summary

Modern knowledge workers switch between too many fragmented tools. Our mission is to build a blazing-fast, distraction-free document editor that combines the real-time fluidity of Google Docs with the modern aesthetic and modularity of Notion.

2. Key Pillars

  • Frictionless Creation: Zero loading delay, instant local-first debounced auto-save, and markdown/docx file ingestion.
  • Granular Collaboration: Transparent document sharing with distinct owner, edit, and view permission boundaries.
  • Rich Formatting Engine: Headings, rich lists, quotes, inline code styling, and clean document export (Markdown, HTML, PDF).

3. Immediate Milestones

  1. Finalize cross-organization permission matrix (Alice & Bob).
  2. Support drag-and-drop file imports for legacy document archives.
  3. Implement version snapshot recovery for asynchronous audit trails.

"Simplicity is prerequisite for reliability." — Edsger W. Dijkstra

Feel free to leave edits or review the permissions in the top right menu.

documents.title: Distributed Document Sync & Conflict Resolution RFC
documents.content:
Distributed Document Sync & CRDT Strategy

Author: Bob Martin (Staff Engineer)

This technical RFC analyzes our state persistence model and outlines the convergence guarantees required for multi-client editing.

1. Problem Statement

When multiple users edit a document concurrently, naive last-write-wins (LWW) strategies can cause keystroke clobbering. We are evaluating structured state synchronization:

  • Operational Transformation (OT): Traditional centralized server model used by Google Docs.
  • Conflict-free Replicated Data Types (CRDTs): Peer-to-peer mergeable data types (e.g. Yjs / Automerge).

2. Technical Architecture

For this product slice, we utilize atomic filesystem transactions with millisecond revision watermarks, paired with client-side optimistic updates and debounced synchronization.

// Example State Snapshot Verification
interface DocumentState {
  revisionId: number;
  contentHash: string;
  lastEditor: string;
}

3. Recommendations

Implement atomic write-ahead logs (WAL) to guarantee document integrity even during unexpected server restarts.

documents.title: Ajaia Design System & Brand Guidelines
documents.content:
Ajaia Design System & Visual Tokens

Author: Charlie Patel (Lead Designer)

These design specifications ensure visual consistency, readability, and accessibility across all productivity tools in the Ajaia workspace.

1. Core Typography

We use Inter for UI and body text, and JetBrains Mono for code blocks and monospace tokens.

2. Color Palette

  • Primary Indigo: #4F46E5 — Primary interactions, focus rings, callouts.
  • Neutral Slate: #0F172A to #F8FAFC — High contrast text and warm canvas backdrops.
  • Emerald Success: #10B981 — Confirmed auto-save and sync checkmarks.
  • Amber Warning: #F59E0B — Unsaved changes or view-only mode notices.

3. Surface Elevation & Shadows

Documents sit on an elevated page card (816px standard width) with a subtle multi-layered diffuse shadow to evoke physical paper while maintaining modern digital lightness.
